title: When Old Expertise Blinds You to Simpler Fixes: The Water-Jar Test
alt_title_2: Why Experienced Pros Miss Obvious One-Step Solutions
description_hook: In 1942, psychologist Abraham Luchins ran his famous water-jar experiments on the Einstellung Effect, showing how learning one complex formula blinded over 80% of subjects to an effortless two-jar shortcut right in front of them.

scenes.headline: How Smart Adults Miss 23 Minus 3 Equals 20
scenes.stat_label: THE OBVIOUS ANSWER HIDDEN BY PRIOR HABIT
bullets: Jars of 23, 49, and 3 quarts to measure 20
Trained experts still took the long 3-jar detour
scenes.narration: How do smart adults miss subtracting three from twenty-three to get twenty? By getting too good at a harder method first.

scenes.headline: Abraham Luchins's 1942 Water-Jar Experiments
bullets: Problems 1-5 needed B minus A minus 2C
On Problem 6, over 80% missed simple A minus C
scenes.narration: In 1942, psychologist Abraham Luchins demonstrated the Einstellung Effect using water-jar puzzles: after five problems required a three-jar formula, over eighty percent of subjects missed an obvious two-jar shortcut right in front of them.
scenes.source: Luchins, 'Mechanization in Problem Solving', Psychological Monographs (1942)

scenes.headline: Yesterday's Playbook Becomes Today's Cage
scenes.left_body: Throws 6-step legacy workflows & agencies at simple tasks
scenes.right_body: Asks 'What is the 1-step path today?' -> solves in 10 lines
scenes.narration: Past career success builds the same mental rut: experienced operators throw complex six-step workflows and pricey agencies at problems a ten-line script solves.

scenes.headline: Luchins's Four-Word Cure: 'Don't Be Blind'
scenes.stat_label: OUTSIDER RESET CUTS UNNECESSARY WORKFLOW STEPS
scenes.stat_subtext: Write 'Don't be blind' at top of page -> test 1-step path first
scenes.narration: Use Luchins's exact cue, 'Don't be blind': before launching your usual playbook, spend five minutes asking how a beginner would solve this in one step.
scenes.source: Abraham S. Luchins (1942), 'Don't be blind' experimental group

scenes.headline: Audit Your Default Formula Before Every Sprint
scenes.stat_label: NEVER AUTOMATE A DETOUR YOU CAN DELETE
bullets: Pause 5 minutes before copying last year's process
Look for the direct 23-minus-3 path first
scenes.narration: Question yesterday's winning formula before every sprint so old expertise never blinds you to simpler leverage.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule based on Abraham Luchins (1942)
